assessment_dispute: ED26-P15-CH-regular-conditional-laws-C002 (A regular conditional law of a random element): the source's non-existence account (Durrett p. 214) is not preserved, and the entry's boundary is not worked. The reader route keeps only the bare report 'the source records that regular conditional distributions do not always exist' (conditioning-independence-and-information-w02b-p15-008.tex lines 235-237). Two things from the source are absent: (a) its attribution of the first example to Dieudonne (1948), with Doob (1953), p. 624, and Faden (1985) for later developments; (b) its explanation that, for disjoint A_n, P(X in U A_n | G) = sum P(X in A_n | G) holds only almost surely, by (4.1.1) and (4.1.3), so the exceptional null sets may pile up when S contains enough countable disjoint collections. The entry also claims (regular-conditional-laws.tex lines 49-51) that the case S = Omega with X the identity needs an existence hypothesis on the outcome space. Nothing on the route demonstrates or supports that claim beyond the bare report. Related text exists only in unrouted files and is not credited.

assessment_dispute: ED26-P15-CH-regular-conditional-laws-C005 (Transport through a Borel real coding): the hypothesis of the source's Theorem 4.1.17 (p. 215) is not preserved. That hypothesis is that (S, S) is nice; the proof restates this as a one-to-one map phi into R with phi and phi^{-1} measurable, with no clause requiring phi(S) to be Borel. The route proves the theorem only for a measurable isomorphism onto a Borel set E (regular-conditional-laws.tex lines 95-110, annex lines 139-181) and calls this 'the source's standard Borel case with its image ... requirements explicit'. It does not state the source's hypothesis in the source's terms. It does not establish the relation to the Borel-image hypothesis: the source's step phi(A) = (phi^{-1})^{-1}(A) in R, for every A, holds exactly when phi(S) is Borel. It also does not settle the theorem for nice spaces whose image is not Borel.

assessment_dispute: ED26-P15-CH-regular-conditional-laws-C007 (Conditional laws parametrized by the observed value): the hypothesis of the source's Theorem 4.1.18 (p. 215) is not preserved. That hypothesis is that X and Y take values in a nice space (S, S) in the source's printed sense, with no Borel-image clause, and G = sigma(Y). The route proves the theorem for X in a Borel-image-coded standard Borel space (regular-conditional-laws.tex lines 133-153, annex lines 183-242) and asserts that the source's theorem 'is included'. It does not state the source's hypothesis, does not relate it to the Borel-image hypothesis (the transport step needs phi(A) Borel for every A, which holds exactly when phi(S) is Borel), and does not settle the case of a non-Borel image.

assessment_dispute: ED26-P15-CH-regular-conditional-laws-C011 (The sphere calculation and two approaches to the same null event): the source's Example 4.1.8 (p. 210) is not presented as the source presents it. Three things are missing. (a) Its name, Borel's paradox. (b) The apparent paradox: for a point chosen uniformly on the globe, one might expect both the new longitude theta in [0, pi), which selects the great circle, and the angle phi in (-pi, pi] along that circle to be uniform, yet theta is uniform and phi is not. (c) The source's resolution, given as its explanation: in either formulation phi is independent of theta, so the conditional distribution is the unconditional one, and that is not uniform because more of the surface lies near the equator than near the North Pole. The route (regular-conditional-laws.tex lines 192-248, annex lines 346-389) supplies the coordinates, the independence, the densities and the nonuniform conditional law, but not (a), (b) or (c).
